name: Tenneco Clean Air India Ltd

profile.what: Indian arm of US-based Tenneco (owned by funds managed or advised by affiliates of Apollo Global Management, AR FY26). Makes exhaust and after-treatment systems (hot end: catalytic converters, DPF/SCR; cold end: mufflers, pipes), powertrain parts (spark plugs, ignition coils, engine bearings, sealings, heat shields) and ride-control products (shock absorbers, struts, DCx DaVinci and semi-active suspension) for Indian car, truck, tractor and off-highway makers, plus a small aftermarket and export business.
profile.marketShare: FY26 value share (CRISIL): CV clean air 58% (#1), off-highway clean air 68% (#1), PV shock absorbers and struts 55% (#1); PV clean air ~20% (Motilal Oswal); engine bearings #2 (CV 34%, PV 44%, FY25).
profile.customersMix: No customer above 22% of VAR; top customer 19.9%, customers 2-5 42.4%, 6-10 16.7% (FY26). Serves all top-7 PV and top-5 CV OEMs; not present in clean air at India's largest (Japanese) PV maker until a CAFE-3 programme expected around FY28-29.

history.event: Tenneco Clean Air India Pvt Ltd incorporated (Tamil Nadu). The Federal-Mogul India ignition, bearings and sealings companies were fellow subsidiaries in the Tenneco group.

Ownership chain (AR FY26): immediate parent Tenneco Mauritius Holdings; ultimate parent Tenneco LLC (Delaware), owned through holding entities by AP IX Pegasus Holdings L.P., i.e. funds managed or advised by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.

Tenneco Automotive India sells Motocare India (aftermarket distribution) to a fellow subsidiary for Rs829 cr; the gain sits in capital reserve on consolidation, the cash was collected in FY26 and paid out as dividends.

Common-control combination: the company acquires Tenneco Automotive India and the three Federal-Mogul India companies (ignition, sealings, bearings) by share swap (189.5 mn new shares); pooled and restated from 1-Apr-2022.
Four interim dividends to Tenneco before the IPO: Rs25.68 a share, Rs1,036.6 cr in total.
Listed on NSE/BSE after a Rs3,600 cr IPO, a pure offer for sale by Tenneco Mauritius Holdings at Rs397 (9.07 cr shares; promoter 97.25% to 74.79%); opened at Rs505 on NSE.
Q3FY26: Rs20.3 cr (post-tax) one-off for the new labour codes (gratuity definition, effective 21-Nov-2025); Kharkhoda (Haryana) Clean Air greenfield announced (Rs71 cr).
Q4FY26: lifetime order book Rs12,400 cr (Mar-2026); western-India ART plant announced (Rs69 cr).
Promoter block sale (floor Rs515; ~Rs525-529 traded; 90-day lock-up on further sales); 9.1 cr shares traded on NSE that day. Reported total sale 6.05 cr shares (15.0% of equity).

ipo.note: Subscription: 61.8x per the company's Q4FY26 presentation; Chittorgarh shows 43.47x (different basis, see conflicts).

q1fy27.capexGuidanceFy27: Rs350-450 cr, 'indicative', fully from internal accruals; includes Rs140 cr for the two announced plants
q1fy27.utilisation: CA&PT above 80%; ART above 90% (Aug-2026); FY26: cold ends 51%, hot ends 78%, shocks 90%
q1fy27.royalty: 2.5% of revenue from operations less intercompany sales, unchanged
q1fy27.recoveries: Customer recoveries and factory productivity +60 bp, already in the margin; steel indexed back-to-back with a one-quarter lag; non-indexed inputs (crude-linked plastics, rubber, LPG/CNG) partly recovered, talks continuing
q1fy27.caGap: CA&PT grew 9.6% against a 16% served market: no exhaust content in EVs (~3-3.5 points) and no presence at the leading Japanese PV OEM, which grew strongly after the GST cut; like-for-like market ~8-10%
q1fy27.wins: Spark-plug order from one of India's largest PV OEMs; PV hot-end programme; CNG cold-end programme for a global OEM; 2.0L after-treatment for a domestic CV maker's SCV range; four new ART customers; DCx32 for A/B-segment cars; maiden ART export order (European ATV maker); heat-shield order from Tenneco America
q1fy27.exportsComment: Export order book ~70% Tenneco-to-Tenneco, ~30% third party; exports 14-20% of new order intake; US tariffs a 'downer' for exhaust-part exports; export margins in line or better than domestic
q1fy27.cashUse: 50-60% of EBITDA converts to cash; options include M&A/inorganic ('wait for the right time')

guidance.text: Order book covers more than 100% of FY28 target revenue; 'healthy double-digit CAGR' (FY25-28), versus 5.9% VAR CAGR FY23-25
Listing costs (management, directors, compliance, legal, IT) make EBITDA 'a bit soft'; to be absorbed with revenue growth and 'come back to the same levels'

CAFE-3 and BS-VII add Rs1,300-1,400 cr of addressable clean-air content (industry); petrol engines with gasoline direct injection need particulate filters from 2027; BS-VII not yet notified ('BS-VI plus or watered-down')
Kharkhoda (Haryana) Clean Air plant Rs71 cr (SoP ~Q3FY27 per JM Financial); western-India ART plant Rs69 cr

relatedParty.royaltyBasis: 2.5% of revenue from operations (including pass-through substrates) less intercompany sales; benchmarked by an independent third party and approved by the independent directors (CFO, Dec-2025)
relatedParty.apa: The group applied for a unilateral APA (FY24-28, rollback FY21-23) on royalty and management-support charges, then filed to withdraw it (AR FY26 consolidated note 45)

management.ceo: Arvind Chandrasekharan (Whole-time Director & CEO since May-2025)
management.board: Eight directors: three independent (Niranjan Kumar Gupta, chairman; Gopika Pant; Jaidit Singh Brar), the CEO, and four non-executive nominees of the parent (Manavendra Singh Sial, Prakash Mahesh, Noah Jesse Falk of Apollo Management from May-2026, Nathan Patrick Bowen). Independent directors are 3 of 8, the legal minimum with an independent chairman (AR FY26 p58-59).

accounting: VAR is a non-GAAP measure: revenue less substrates; margins quoted on VAR look ~1.7 points higher than on reported revenue.
FY23-FY26 are pooled (common-control) restated figures, not the shell's history; FY21-22 dropped from the model.

FY26 operating cash flow (Rs1,429 cr) includes collection of the Rs829 cr Motocare sale consideration (Screener 'other working-capital items' +Rs663 cr); the company's own FCF/EBITDA (58%) excludes it.
Q1FY26 profit included a one-off from the Motocare sale and other one-off income; Q3FY26 a Rs27 cr pre-tax (Rs20 cr post-tax) labour-code charge.
